claims.text: The one fact the fee turns on beyond the driver's own trace — where the rider was — is left in direct conflict by two admissible artifacts. The chat_log has the rider telling the driver at 16:08:02 'coming coming 2 min', a statement that she was on her way to the pickup, while the rider's own track in the same bundle places her device between 633.9 m and 646.4 m from the pickup pin and never moving (the only speed recorded is 0.0) for the whole window from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20. No clause resolves that conflict: POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-02 read the driver's track only; POL-NS-03 is confined to a driver stationary outside the 120 m arrival radius, which this driver was not; and POL-NS-04 never reaches its rider-presence test at all, because limb (b) fails — the driver replied 18 seconds after the rider's message (16:08:20) and placed an answered 0:34 in-app call at 16:09:40, so subsection (c) is not run. With the record irreconcilable on rider presence and no operative clause to break the tie, the honest disposition is that the fee is held rather than collected: escalate under POL-NS-09.

The venue comparison POL-NS-03 depends on cannot be run on this record at all, and that gap is what the reviewer must close. The pickup pin — 'The Interlace, Main Guardhouse, 180 Depot Rd' — carries venue_id null, and not one message in the chat_log names an entrance, gate, block, tower or bay, so neither party's statement nor any venue_id can establish that the driver's held position and the rider's stationary device were ever the same pickup face; POL-NS-03 forbids anyone, advocate or judge, from asserting that identity from general geography. With registered_pickup_points of 2 at this LARGE_VENUE, the record leaves open precisely the question the distance test was written to answer, which is a further reason for POL-NS-09 escalation rather than an automated monetary ruling in either direction.

The charge stands or falls on the four conjunctive conditions of POL-NS-01, each of which must be proved on this trip's own artifacts. Under POL-GEN-01 neither the driver's 1,706 lifetime trips and 4.9 rating, nor the rider's lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags, may ground any finding about this trip; only the trailing-window fields that the clauses actually name may be used, and only for the test that names them. The rider asks the judge to decide on EV-GPS-00208, EV-CHAT-00208 and EV-FARE-00208 alone, and to discard any reasoning built on reputation.

The rider does not dispute the dwell arithmetic, and does not argue POL-NS-05 or POL-NS-06 on it: the derived facts give a single continuous in-geofence run of 585 seconds, 285 seconds beyond the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 16:02:10 and therefore already underway when the 'arrived' marker was set at 16:02:25. The rider's case does not rest on that limb. It rests on the question the record leaves open — whether the rider and the driver were ever directed to the same pickup face — and on the fact that the rider's device was stationary throughout, which is consistent with a rider waiting where she believed she had been told to wait rather than with a rider evading the pickup.

EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING — it has no payload and carries weight 0.0 — and its absence is itself citable: there is no traffic advisory of any type covering this pickup road or this waiting period, so the driver cannot bring himself within POL-NS-06(i) to accumulate or extend the wait, and there is no external record at all of the kerbside conditions against which the driver's account of the hold can be checked. The rider relies on the absence, not on any content.

The driver's own GPS trace satisfies every limb of the baseline chargeable no-show under POL-NS-01. Limb (a): trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25. Limb (b): the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds BEFORE that event, so the 'inside the geofence at or before the arrived timestamp' test is met with room to spare. Limb (c): the driver then held position inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for a single continuous run of 585 seconds, almost double the 300 second minimum for that zone class. Limb (d): trip_record shows no boarding event (started_at and ended_at are both null) and the trip terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 16:11:55. All four limbs hold and the fee is legitimately chargeable.

Arrival is established under POL-NS-02 on admissible fixes, not on the driver's say-so. The trace yields 60 qualifying in-radius fixes, each falling inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for this condominium pickup zone and each passing the 25 m horizontal-accuracy filter, with the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin at 28.78 m. That is far more than the three consecutive qualifying fixes the proximity test requires. The zone class comes from trip_record.pickup_zone_class, not from assumption.

This is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case under POL-NS-03, and POL-NS-03 therefore cannot displace the fee. That clause only governs where the driver was stationary for the required dwell OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin. The driver's qualifying run sits inside the 120 m radius the whole time, so the 400 m ceiling is never reached and the venue-identity corroboration question never arises. The rider's 'he never came at all' is answered by a trace that puts the vehicle within 29 m of her own pickup pin for nearly ten minutes.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival marker test is not engaged on this record. The qualifying in-geofence run begins at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds before the 'arrived' event, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 28.78 m — nowhere near the clause's 300 m threshold — so the driver was not marking arrival from an expressway or an arterial road. Even if the marker were somehow impugned, limb (iii) of POL-NS-05 preserves the fee: the corrected dwell, recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, is 585 seconds and still clears the 300 second minimum, so POL-NS-01 governs the outcome.

POL-NS-06's waiting-period shortfall route is closed on the arithmetic. The effective in-geofence dwell is 585 seconds against a LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 seconds, and the derived shortfall is MINUS 285 seconds — a surplus of four minutes and forty-five seconds, not a deficit. There is nothing to refund under this clause, and the strict-liability rationale the clause rests on (that the rider paid for a full five-minute wait) was in fact honoured and exceeded.

The rider cannot shelter under POL-NS-04, because limb (b) of that clause is affirmatively failed. Limb (b) requires that the driver neither posted a chat reply within 120 seconds of the rider's message nor placed an in-app voice call before terminating. The rider's only message, 'coming coming 2 min', was sent at 16:08:02; the driver replied 'ok no problem' at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds later, and he placed an in-app voice call at 16:09:40 which the rider answered and which ran 34 seconds. The rider was not left in silence by an unresponsive driver — the record shows the opposite.

POL-NS-04 limb (c) also fails, and it fails affirmatively rather than being undecidable, so the clause does not apply on any of its three limbs. The rider's track is present in the trace and carries 141 fixes, but ZERO of them qualify inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius: her device sat stationary (distinct speed 0.0 kph) at a mean distance of 639.84 m from the pickup pin for the whole window, from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20. A rider who is 640 m from the pin the entire time is not a rider who was at the pin coordinating a pickup.

The rider's account — that the driver 'never came at all' — is contradicted by the chat log the rider herself participated in. The driver messaged at 16:02:40 identifying himself and his vehicle, 'hello ma'am i'm at the main guardhouse, white Honda Vezel SJK8842P'. The rider READ that message at 16:03:01. The driver chased again at 16:07:15, 'ma'am? still here waiting ah', which the rider read at 16:07:29, and she then replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02. A rider who reads a driver's plate number and guardhouse location and answers 'coming' is not a rider confronting an absent vehicle; the six-message log corroborates the driver's version and not the claim text.

The rider's assertion that she 'called him also cannot get through' has nothing behind it in the record. trip_record.in_app_calls records exactly one call on this trip — placed BY THE DRIVER at 16:09:40, answered, duration 34 seconds. No rider-placed call appears anywhere in the telemetry, and the chat log's VOICE_CALL_LOG entry is the driver's call, not hers. The counterparty statement that she 'picked up and said' she was coming also matches that single recorded answered call.

The $8.00 charge is arithmetically correct and discloses no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee: the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee is SGD 8.00, so SGD 8.00 governs, and the tier dimension (not the zone dimension) is what produced the figure. The fare_breakdown cancellation_fee line is exactly SGD 8.00, the schedule fee resolves to SGD 8.00, and the derived difference is 0.00. The rider's complaint about the AMOUNT of the charge has no purchase either.

The driver's compensation follows under POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the itemised fee: SGD 6.40 of the SGD 8.00 charged, with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee, matching the derived driver_compensation figure exactly. The anti-farming guard does not trip and requires BOTH limbs to trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, an order of magnitude below the 0.08 rate limb. Compensation is therefore payable rather than withheld, and no escalation under POL-NS-09 is triggered on this check.

No escalation trigger is open on the profile counters, so this case is decidable on the money rather than held. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so the 'two or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver' test in POL-NS-09(c) is not met. Nothing in the admissible bundle contradicts anything else on arrival, dwell or rider presence: the trip record's 9.8 minute wait, the trace's 585 second run and the 16:12:10 termination all line up.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING and carries no payload, so it cannot be used by anyone. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable, and its absence is citable as absence: it neither excuses a shortfall nor permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed. The driver does not need it — his 585 second dwell is a single continuous qualifying run (run_count 1) that already clears the 300 second minimum on its own — so the missing artifact does not touch the outcome and must not be read as evidence against him.

The rider's timeline is not supported by the platform's own timestamps, which matters because her claim turns on how long she waited for a car that never came. The trip record shows the driver 'arrived' at 16:02:25 and the trip cancelled at 16:12:10 — a waiting window of 9 minutes 45 seconds, not 'almost 15 minutes'. The whole booking, from request at 15:51:55 to cancellation, is 20 minutes 15 seconds. The driver's own account ('nearly ten minutes') matches the telemetry; the rider's does not.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 8.00 no-show fee stands, and the driver is compensated SGD 6.40 of it.

WHY THE FEE STANDS (POL-NS-01). The fee is chargeable only if four conditions hold, and on this trip all four do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25. (b) The GPS trace's first qualifying fix inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for the pickup pin is at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds BEFORE that event, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 28.78 m — comfortably inside (POL-NS-02; 60 qualifying in-radius fixes, well over the three required). (c) The driver then held position in one continuous in-geofence run of 585 seconds (16:02:10 to 16:11:55), clearing the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum by 285 seconds. (d) The trip record shows no boarding (started_at and ended_at are both null) and the trip was terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell had elapsed.

No clause displaces it. POL-NS-03 governs only a driver held stationary OUTSIDE the arrival radius; this driver was inside it, so the clause and its 400 m venue test are never reached. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's 16:08:02 message within 18 seconds ('ok no problem', 16:08:20) and placed an answered 34-second in-app call at 16:09:40, so limb (b) fails, and limb (c) fails affirmatively — 0 of the rider's 141 fixes fall inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-05 is not engaged (the marker was set inside the radius, not from an expressway or arterial road), and its limb (iii) would preserve the fee anyway, since the corrected dwell still clears the minimum. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to work on: 585 seconds against 300 seconds, a surplus of 285, not a deficit.

WHY THE RIDER'S ACCOUNT DOES NOT CHANGE THIS. The claim that the driver 'never came at all' is met by a trace putting his vehicle within about 29 m of her own pickup pin for nearly ten minutes, and by a chat log she read: the driver's 16:02:40 message naming the main guardhouse and his plate (read 16:03:01), his 16:07:15 follow-up (read 16:07:29), and her reply 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02. Her 'called him also cannot get through' has nothing behind it — the only call recorded on the trip is the driver's, at 16:09:40, answered, 34 seconds. Her 'almost 15 minutes' does not match the platform's own timestamps: arrival (16:02:25) to cancellation (16:12:10) is 9 minutes 45 seconds, which matches the driver's account, not hers. On this record her own device sat stationary about 640 m from the pin from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20.

The amount is right. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the charge is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), so the vehicle-tier dimension produced the SGD 8.00; the fare line reconciles exactly (derived difference 0.00, no POL-NS-08(d) defect).

WHY THE DRIVER IS PAID. POL-NS-07 compensates at 80 percent of the itemised fee: SGD 6.40 of SGD 8.00, the residual SGD 1.60 retained as the platform service fee, matching the derived figure. The anti-farming check does not trip — it requires BOTH no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a rate above 0.08; the figures are 2 and 2/143 = 0.014.

ON THE ESCALATION ARGUMENT (POL-NS-09). I have considered the submission that the chat log and the rider's GPS track conflict on rider presence and that no clause resolves it. I do not accept it. Rider presence is not a limb of the clause that decides this case — POL-NS-01 reads the driver's arrival, dwell and termination, not the rider's location — so no deciding fact is left in conflict. The clause that does read rider presence, POL-NS-04(c), is not reached because limb (b) fails, and its test would fail affirmatively in any event (0 of 141 rider fixes inside 150 m). Nor does the rider's message contradict her track: 'coming in 2 min' is consistent with a rider who never reached the pin. No POL-NS-09 trigger is open — confidence is at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; the profile counters do not meet limbs (c) or (d) (both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1); and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) (no clock skew beyond 90 seconds, no gap over 120 seconds and 120 fixes present, chat message count 6 matches the trip record, fare reconciles). No clause produces a referral: no false-arrival record is due under POL-NS-05(ii), and the POL-NS-07 escalation packet is not triggered.

TWO FURTHER POINTS. EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so it can carry no fact; its absence neither helps nor hurts the driver — he does not need POL-NS-06(i) accumulation, because his dwell is a single continuous 585-second run. And no profile has been used to establish anything about this trip: POL-GEN-01 makes rating, lifetime trips, prior_no_show_flags and the like context only, and I have not relied on them for either party.

Outcome: the filing party's claim is not supported, the SGD 8.00 charge stands as it is, and the driver is paid SGD 6.40.

ruling.explanation:
This case was decided on the platform's own records, and both accounts were tested against them.

To the rider: the driver did come. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00208) and trip record (EV-TRIP-00208) show he reached the pickup point 'The Interlace, Main Guardhouse, 180 Depot Rd' at 16:02:25 on 30 July 2026 and then held position there for a continuous 585 seconds (9 min 45 s), from his first in-geofence fix at 16:02:10 to 16:11:55. That is 60 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup, all passing the 25 m accuracy filter, with his closest approach 28.78 m from the pin. The required hold for a large-venue pickup is 300 seconds, so he waited 285 seconds longer than required. All four conditions of POL-NS-01 are met: (a) the trip record carries the 'arrived' event at 16:02:25; (b) the trace places him inside the geofence at 16:02:10, before that event; (c) the 585-second dwell exceeds the 300-second minimum; and (d) no boarding took place and he terminated the trip at 16:12:10 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell elapsed. Nothing displaces the fee: the driver was inside the arrival radius, so POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) is never reached; POL-NS-05 (false marker) is not engaged because at the marker he was stationary 28.78 m from the pin, nowhere near the 300 m threshold; and the dwell was a surplus, not a shortfall, so POL-NS-06 does not apply. Your statement that the driver 'never came at all' is contradicted by the chat log (EV-CHAT-00208): you read his message naming his car and the main guardhouse at 16:03:01 and replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02. Your statement that you 'called him also cannot get through' has nothing behind it: the only call recorded is one the driver placed at 16:09:40, which you answered, lasting 34 seconds. Your own device track shows you 633.9 to 646.4 m from the pickup pin and never moving through the window; but because the fee turns on the driver doing his part at the pin, and he did, that does not change the outcome.

Your request to escalate is declined. POL-NS-09(b) needs two admissible artifacts in direct contradiction on arrival, dwell or rider presence that no clause resolves. The chat log and your track do not directly contradict each other — you said you were coming, and your track shows you did not arrive — and rider presence decides no operative limb here, since POL-NS-04 is disposed of on its limb (b), which fails because the driver replied 18 seconds later and then placed an answered in-app call. The other counters do not fire either: no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0.

To the driver: your POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-04, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 claims are accepted, as is your point that the rider's '15 minutes' timeline is not supported (the waiting window was 9 min 45 s, and your account of 'nearly ten minutes' matches the telemetry). The $8.00 charge is correct: under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the fee is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), and the vehicle tier produces the SGD 8.00 charged in EV-FARE-00208, which reconciles exactly (difference 0.00). Under POL-NS-07 you are compensated at 80% of the SGD 8.00 fee = SGD 6.40, with SGD 1.60 retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check (POL-NS-07/POL-GEN-01) does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below the absolute threshold of 4) and 2/143 = 0.014 (below the 0.08 rate limb), so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

On the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 (no payload, weight 0.0): its absence is noted and changes nothing. Your dwell was a single continuous qualifying run that already clears the minimum, so the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation limb was never needed and no one is exonerated or penalised by the absence.

No artifact deciding this case is impaired under POL-NS-08: no clock skew (the arrived event sits 15 seconds from the first qualifying fix), no sampling gap (max gap 0.0 s across 120 fixes), the chat log is complete at 6 messages matching the trip record, and the fee reconciles to the schedule. The finding accordingly rests on EV-GPS-00208, EV-TRIP-00208 and EV-FARE-00208 at full weight, and confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. Nothing a clause produces a referral for, so the referrals list is empty; the only open question — whether the rider was waiting at a different face of the venue — is recorded here for the reader and is not a clause-mandated instruction.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your claim that the driver never came is contradicted by the platform's own records. The driver's GPS trace places his vehicle inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE condominium pickup from 16:02:10, with 60 qualifying in-radius fixes and a closest approach of 28.8 m to your pickup pin. He then held that position in one continuous run of 585 seconds (9 min 45 s) against the 300-second minimum for a large venue, ending at 16:11:55, and cancelled at 16:12:10 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. He also messaged you at 16:02:40 giving his plate (SJK8842P) and the main guardhouse, which you read at 16:03:01; he chased at 16:07:15; you replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02; and you answered his 34-second in-app call at 16:09:40. Your assertion that you called him and could not get through has nothing behind it: the only call on the trip was placed by the driver, and it was answered. Your own device sat stationary between 633.9 m and 646.4 m from the pickup pin for the whole window (15:54:00 to 16:15:20), and your timeline of 'almost 15 minutes' does not match the platform's 9 min 45 s whose telemetry the driver's own account matches. All four conditions of POL-NS-01 therefore hold, and none of the clauses that could displace the fee applies. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m; this driver was inside the 120 m radius, so it does not apply and the venue-comparison gap the rider's advocate raises never arises. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (b) because the driver replied 18 seconds after your message and placed an answered call, and its rider-presence limb also fails affirmatively on the track. POL-NS-05 is not engaged (about 29 m from the pin, not 300 m, and not travelling at 15 km/h), and its limb (iii) would preserve the fee anyway. POL-NS-06 shows a surplus, not a shortfall: 585 s against 300 s, i.e. plus 285 s. The $8.00 charge is arithmetically correct: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) is SGD 8.00, produced by the vehicle-tier dimension, and the fare breakdown reconciles exactly (difference 0.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. To the driver: because POL-NS-01 is satisfied and nothing displaces it, POL-NS-07 pays you 80 percent of the SGD 8.00 fee, i.e. SGD 6.40, with SGD 1.60 (20 percent) retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip, and both limbs are required: your no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 2 divided by 143 completed trips is 0.014, far below the 0.08 rate limb. The ruling is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 6.40 and, under POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd carries the same figure: it is the amount this ruling moves, not a refund to the filing party, and the rider's charge stands as it presently is. I have rejected the rider's call to escalate. The tension its advocate points to - the 'coming coming 2 min' message against the rider's own stationary track 640 m away - is not a contradiction between two admissible artifacts on a fact this decision turns on, and it is answered by the rider's own track and by the fact that a no-show fee is chargeable whether or not the rider reached the pin. No POL-NS-09 trigger is open: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the profile counters read no_show_disputes_30d of 1 (below 3) and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 for both parties (below 2), and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) - no clock skew (the 16:02:25 arrival marker sits seconds from the trace's 10 s cadence and the 16:12:10 termination matches), no trace gap (max gap 0 s, 120 fixes), the chat is complete (6 of 6 messages with no gap over 5 minutes), and the fare reconciles. On profiling, nothing here is decided on reputation: the driver's lifetime trips and rating and the rider's prior_no_show_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and I have used none of them; the only profile fields used are the ones the clauses name - no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d for POL-NS-07, and the two disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields for POL-NS-09(c). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING and carries no fact; it is cited only for its absence, and because the driver's dwell is a single continuous run rather than summed intervals, that absence changes nothing. Finally, I cannot order a callback to the rider: no clause provides for one, so it appears in this explanation and not as a referral.

To the rider: your claim that the driver never came is not supported by this trip's own telemetry. The GPS trace places the driver's vehicle inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE condominium pickup continuously for 585 seconds (9 min 45 s), from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55, with a closest approach of 28.78 m to the pickup pin and 60 fixes passing the 25 m accuracy filter. His 'arrived' marker at 16:02:25 came 15 seconds after he was already inside the geofence, and he cancelled at 16:12:10 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding ever recorded. All four conditions of POL-NS-01 therefore hold and the $8.00 fee is chargeable. The waiting-period route in POL-NS-06 does not help you: the measured dwell of 585 s exceeds the 300 s LARGE_VENUE minimum by 285 s, so there is no shortfall to refund. POL-NS-05's false-arrival test is not engaged — the driver was 28.78 m from the pin, not more than 300 m, and stationary. Your account that you 'called him also cannot get through' is not in the record: the only call on this trip is one the driver placed at 16:09:40, answered, lasting 34 seconds, with no rider-placed call anywhere. Your own device telemetry shows it stationary at about 640 m from the pickup pin for the whole window, so the record does not support your description of waiting at the guardhouse, nor your 'almost 15 minutes' (the platform's own timestamps give 9 min 45 s from the 16:02:25 arrival to the 16:12:10 cancellation). The $8.00 amount is also correct: it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), the vehicle tier producing the figure, and the fare line reconciles exactly.

To the driver: your compensation is payable under POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the itemised $8.00 fee, which is $6.40, with $1.60 (20 percent) retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming guard does not trip and needs both limbs: your no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by 143 completed trips is 0.014, well below the 0.08 rate limb. No escalation under POL-NS-09 is triggered.

On the rider's escalation argument under POL-NS-09(b): I do not accept that two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence. The driver's trace on arrival and dwell is uncontradicted, and the only artifact measuring rider presence is the rider track itself; the chat message 'coming coming 2 min' is a statement by a party, not an independent measurement, and does not contradict the track. In any event the charge under POL-NS-01 does not turn on rider presence at all, so the alleged conflict decides nothing. No other escalation trigger applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, no_show_disputes_30d is 1, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) — the arrived event sits 15 s from the nearest trace fix (well under 90 s), there is no trace gap (max gap 0 s, 120 driver and 141 rider fixes with the rider track present), the chat log holds all 6 messages its msg_id sequence and the trip record's chat_message_count require with no 5-minute gap, and the fare line equals the schedule resolution. POL-NS-03 is not engaged: it governs only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m, whereas this driver was inside the radius throughout and the rider's device was about 640 m away, so there is no venue-identity question to answer. POL-NS-04 does not apply either: limb (b) fails because the driver replied 18 seconds after the rider's message and placed an answered in-app call before terminating, and limb (c) fails because none of the 141 rider fixes fell within the 150 m presence radius. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 (weight 0.0, no payload) carries nothing and is citable only as absence; the driver does not need it, because his dwell is already a single continuous qualifying run. Finally, per POL-GEN-01 no profile field was used to ground any finding about this trip: the driver's lifetime trips and rating and the rider's lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags are context only and were not relied on, and the only profile fields used (no_show_terminations_30d, completed_trips_30d, no_show_disputes_30d, disputes_with_counterparty_90d) were used solely for the POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09 tests that name them.

The rider asks the judge to decide on EV-GPS-00208, EV-CHAT-00208 and EV-FARE-00208 alone, and to discard any reasoning built on reputation.

ledger.claim: The one fact the fee turns on beyond the driver's own trace — where the rider was — is left in direct conflict by two admissible artifacts. The chat_log has the rider telling the driver at 16:08:02 'coming coming 2 min', a statement that she was on her way to the pickup, while the rider's own track in the same bundle places her device between 633.9 m and 646.4 m from the pickup pin and never moving (the only speed recorded is 0.0) for the whole window from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20. No clause resolves that conflict: POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-02 read the driver's track only; POL-NS-03 is confined to a driver stationary outside the 120 m arrival radius, which this driver was not; and POL-NS-04 never reaches its rider-presence test at all, because limb (b) fails — the driver replied 18 seconds after the rider's message (16:08:20) and placed an answered 0:34 in-app call at 16:09:40, so subsection (c) is not run. With the record irreconcilable on rider presence and no operative clause to break the tie, the honest disposition is that the fee is held rather than collected: escalate under POL-NS-09.

The venue comparison POL-NS-03 depends on cannot be run on this record at all, and that gap is what the reviewer must close. The pickup pin — 'The Interlace, Main Guardhouse, 180 Depot Rd' — carries venue_id null, and not one message in the chat_log names an entrance, gate, block, tower or bay, so neither party's statement nor any venue_id can establish that the driver's held position and the rider's stationary device were ever the same pickup face; POL-NS-03 forbids anyone, advocate or judge, from asserting that identity from general geography. With registered_pickup_points of 2 at this LARGE_VENUE, the record leaves open precisely the question the distance test was written to answer, which is a further reason for POL-NS-09 escalation rather than an automated monetary ruling in either direction.

The charge stands or falls on the four conjunctive conditions of POL-NS-01, each of which must be proved on this trip's own artifacts. Under POL-GEN-01 neither the driver's 1,706 lifetime trips and 4.9 rating, nor the rider's lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags, may ground any finding about this trip; only the trailing-window fields that the clauses actually name may be used, and only for the test that names them. ledger.claim: The rider does not dispute the dwell arithmetic, and does not argue POL-NS-05 or POL-NS-06 on it: the derived facts give a single continuous in-geofence run of 585 seconds, 285 seconds beyond the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 16:02:10 and therefore already underway when the 'arrived' marker was set at 16:02:25. The rider's case does not rest on that limb. It rests on the question the record leaves open — whether the rider and the driver were ever directed to the same pickup face — and on the fact that the rider's device was stationary throughout, which is consistent with a rider waiting where she believed she had been told to wait rather than with a rider evading the pickup.

EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING — it has no payload and carries weight 0.0 — and its absence is itself citable: there is no traffic advisory of any type covering this pickup road or this waiting period, so the driver cannot bring himself within POL-NS-06(i) to accumulate or extend the wait, and there is no external record at all of the kerbside conditions against which the driver's account of the hold can be checked. The rider relies on the absence, not on any content.

The driver's own GPS trace satisfies every limb of the baseline chargeable no-show under POL-NS-01. Limb (a): trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25. Limb (b): the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds BEFORE that event, so the 'inside the geofence at or before the arrived timestamp' test is met with room to spare. Limb (c): the driver then held position inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for a single continuous run of 585 seconds, almost double the 300 second minimum for that zone class. Limb (d): trip_record shows no boarding event (started_at and ended_at are both null) and the trip terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 16:11:55. All four limbs hold and the fee is legitimately chargeable.

Arrival is established under POL-NS-02 on admissible fixes, not on the driver's say-so. The trace yields 60 qualifying in-radius fixes, each falling inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for this condominium pickup zone and each passing the 25 m horizontal-accuracy filter, with the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin at 28.78 m. That is far more than the three consecutive qualifying fixes the proximity test requires. The zone class comes from trip_record.pickup_zone_class, not from assumption.

This is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case under POL-NS-03, and POL-NS-03 therefore cannot displace the fee. That clause only governs where the driver was stationary for the required dwell OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin. The driver's qualifying run sits inside the 120 m radius the whole time, so the 400 m ceiling is never reached and the venue-identity corroboration question never arises. The rider's 'he never came at all' is answered by a trace that puts the vehicle within 29 m of her own pickup pin for nearly ten minutes.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival marker test is not engaged on this record. The qualifying in-geofence run begins at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds before the 'arrived' event, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 28.78 m — nowhere near the clause's 300 m threshold — so the driver was not marking arrival from an expressway or an arterial road. Even if the marker were somehow impugned, limb (iii) of POL-NS-05 preserves the fee: the corrected dwell, recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, is 585 seconds and still clears the 300 second minimum, so POL-NS-01 governs the outcome.

POL-NS-06's waiting-period shortfall route is closed on the arithmetic. The effective in-geofence dwell is 585 seconds against a LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 seconds, and the derived shortfall is MINUS 285 seconds — a surplus of four minutes and forty-five seconds, not a deficit. There is nothing to refund under this clause, and the strict-liability rationale the clause rests on (that the rider paid for a full five-minute wait) was in fact honoured and exceeded.

The rider cannot shelter under POL-NS-04, because limb (b) of that clause is affirmatively failed. Limb (b) requires that the driver neither posted a chat reply within 120 seconds of the rider's message nor placed an in-app voice call before terminating. The rider's only message, 'coming coming 2 min', was sent at 16:08:02; the driver replied 'ok no problem' at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds later, and he placed an in-app voice call at 16:09:40 which the rider answered and which ran 34 seconds. The rider was not left in silence by an unresponsive driver — the record shows the opposite.

POL-NS-04 limb (c) also fails, and it fails affirmatively rather than being undecidable, so the clause does not apply on any of its three limbs. The rider's track is present in the trace and carries 141 fixes, but ZERO of them qualify inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius: her device sat stationary (distinct speed 0.0 kph) at a mean distance of 639.84 m from the pickup pin for the whole window, from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20. A rider who is 640 m from the pin the entire time is not a rider who was at the pin coordinating a pickup.

The rider's account — that the driver 'never came at all' — is contradicted by the chat log the rider herself participated in. The driver messaged at 16:02:40 identifying himself and his vehicle, 'hello ma'am i'm at the main guardhouse, white Honda Vezel SJK8842P'. The rider READ that message at 16:03:01. The driver chased again at 16:07:15, 'ma'am? still here waiting ah', which the rider read at 16:07:29, and she then replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02. A rider who reads a driver's plate number and guardhouse location and answers 'coming' is not a rider confronting an absent vehicle; the six-message log corroborates the driver's version and not the claim text.

The rider's assertion that she 'called him also cannot get through' has nothing behind it in the record. trip_record.in_app_calls records exactly one call on this trip — placed BY THE DRIVER at 16:09:40, answered, duration 34 seconds. No rider-placed call appears anywhere in the telemetry, and the chat log's VOICE_CALL_LOG entry is the driver's call, not hers. The counterparty statement that she 'picked up and said' she was coming also matches that single recorded answered call.

The $8.00 charge is arithmetically correct and discloses no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee: the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee is SGD 8.00, so SGD 8.00 governs, and the tier dimension (not the zone dimension) is what produced the figure. The fare_breakdown cancellation_fee line is exactly SGD 8.00, the schedule fee resolves to SGD 8.00, and the derived difference is 0.00. The rider's complaint about the AMOUNT of the charge has no purchase either.

The driver's compensation follows under POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the itemised fee: SGD 6.40 of the SGD 8.00 charged, with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee, matching the derived driver_compensation figure exactly. The anti-farming guard does not trip and requires BOTH limbs to trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, an order of magnitude below the 0.08 rate limb. Compensation is therefore payable rather than withheld, and no escalation under POL-NS-09 is triggered on this check.

No escalation trigger is open on the profile counters, so this case is decidable on the money rather than held. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so the 'two or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver' test in POL-NS-09(c) is not met. Nothing in the admissible bundle contradicts anything else on arrival, dwell or rider presence: the trip record's 9.8 minute wait, the trace's 585 second run and the 16:12:10 termination all line up.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING and carries no payload, so it cannot be used by anyone. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable, and its absence is citable as absence: it neither excuses a shortfall nor permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed. The driver does not need it — his 585 second dwell is a single continuous qualifying run (run_count 1) that already clears the 300 second minimum on its own — so the missing artifact does not touch the outcome and must not be read as evidence against him.

The rider's timeline is not supported by the platform's own timestamps, which matters because her claim turns on how long she waited for a car that never came. The trip record shows the driver 'arrived' at 16:02:25 and the trip cancelled at 16:12:10 — a waiting window of 9 minutes 45 seconds, not 'almost 15 minutes'. The whole booking, from request at 15:51:55 to cancellation, is 20 minutes 15 seconds. The driver's own account ('nearly ten minutes') matches the telemetry; the rider's does not.
